title: Dextran Labeling and Uptake in Live and Functional Murine Cochlear Hair Cells
protocol: Set up breeding pairs of C57BL/6J wild-type mice in the animal facility.
Monitor the date of birth of litters and track the age of pups.
Clean the dissection space with 70% ethanol.
Place a clean bench pad for dissection.
Prepare several 35 mm dishes with Leibovitz's L15 media.
Euthanize postnatal-day-6 (P6) mice by decapitation.
Use surgical scissors to remove the skin of the skull by making a superficial cut from the anterior to the posterior end and across the external auditory canals.
Fold the skin towards the nose to expose the cranium.
Make an incision from the back to the front of the skull and across the eye line.
Separate the skull in two halves and remove the brain with the use of a small spatula to expose the temporal bones.
With small scissors, cut around the temporal bones, and excise the tissue.
Place both temporal bones in a 35 mm dish and make sure they are covered with L15 media.

Remove the surrounding cochleae tissue, semicircular canals, and vestibular organs with surgical forceps under a stereomicroscope equipped with a widefield eyepiece (a 10X magnification power) and an external alternating current halogen light source.
Perform two puncture bounds on the dissected cochleae, one on the round window and another at the apical cochlear region.
Reconstitute dextran in HBSS-CFM at a final concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Aliquot the dextran stock solution in opaque black tubes and store at -30°C.
Prepare each dextran at a final concentration of 2 mg/mL in 500 mL Leibovitz's L15 media.
Remove the media from the cochlea and add Leibovitz's L15 media containing dextran at a final concentration of 2 mg/mL.
Incubate with gentle shaking (25 rpm) on a 3-dimensional shaker tilted at 25° for 2 h at room temperature.
Place the 9-well glass plate inside a cell culture P150 dish wrapped in aluminum foil during incubation to protect from light.
Wash the tissue twice for 2 min each and once with HBSS after incubation.
Incubate the tissue at room temperature for 30 min with 4% paraformaldehyde in HBSS.
Quickly and gently wash the fixed tissue twice with HBSS to remove paraformaldehyde.
Remove the spiral ligament and tectorial membrane with fine tip forceps to dissect the organ of Corti.
Wash the tissue with HBSS.
Permeabilize the tissue in 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS containing fluorescently-labeled phalloidin at a 1:200 dilution for 30 min to label F-actin and visualize actin-based stereocilia.
Wash the tissue 2–3 times for 2 min each time with HBSS buffer to remove excess triton and phalloidin, and once with PBS to remove salts.
Mount the organ of Corti tissues on a microscope slide and cover it with mounting media.
Aspirate any bubble generated during the addition of the mounting media with a pipette.
Place an edge of the coverslip close to the sample and carefully lower it over the tissue using forceps or a pipette tip.
Incubate the mounted tissue overnight at room temperature to let the mounting media dry.
Store the slides at 4 °C until imaging.
Add a small drop of immersion oil on the objective.
Place the microscope slide containing the mounted tissue sample in the microscope stage with the glass coverslip facing the immersion oil.
Set imaging parameters using the image acquisition software.
Use identical image acquisition settings for x, y, and z resolution in each experiment.
Collect a z-stack of images from stereocilia to the apical half of the hair cell body.
Use a piezo-driven focus system to move the objective precisely during imaging.
Process raw confocal images using the Airyscan 3D reconstruction algorithm.
Adjust brightness and contrast of processed images using image processing software.
Add scale bar to the images in the image processing software.
Export processed images for final figures.
